ex.en: I take a walk along the river every evening.
We ate fried chicken by the Han River on the weekend.
This river is dangerous for swimming.

fix.en: to be old, be a long time
fix.note: As a modifier: 오래된 집 = an old house.

ex.en: It's been a long time since we've seen each other.

fix.note: 기대돼요 = I'm looking forward to it, I'm excited.

ex.en: I'm really looking forward to the weekend trip.
Don't get your hopes up too much.
I'll be looking forward to my birthday present.

fix.note: 기억이 안 나요 = I can't remember.

ex.en: Be sure to remember the appointment time.
Do you remember the day we first met?

fix.note: Casual; also 너희들. Polite plural: 여러분. 너희 엄마 = your mom, even to one friend.

ex.en: Your mom is such a good cook.
Kids, did you all finish your homework?

ex.s: 언어를 몇 개 할 수 있어요?
ex.en: How many languages can you speak?
Korean is a really fun language.
Practice is important when learning a language.

notes: Examples using a different lemma (기대돼요, 기억이 나다) replaced; 오래되다 is an adjective; compound-only 강 example; unnatural 몇 개 언어; 너희 note clarified.
